answer: Conductance-throttled pearl routing: each transaction carries a pearl probe; a random raven verifier routes it over two edge-disjoint paths through the interaction graph. If both paths remain inside a dense vine of mutual links with low external conductance, the agent’s throughput is capped. Attack cost: a sybil cluster must maintain many diverse cross-cluster edges into honest regions, adding real latency, bandwidth, and edge-maintenance overhead per node—internal links alone do not lift the cap.
